        #LearnerActive days, all time

          EOR Rating

          Current ranks learners by their standing EOR Rating, a practice score that starts at 1200.

          EOR Rating is an Elo-style score that starts at 1200. Each rated result is a game against an opponent rating: AI quiz questions count as 1000 (basic), 1200 (standard) or 1400 (challenge), duels use the other player's rating, and weekend events use a 1500-rated opponent. Beating a stronger opponent gains more; losing to a weaker one costs more.

          Duels move the rating further than practice, and a ten-question weekend Quiz Sprint weighs the same as five games, settled after the event closes. Historical puzzle results keep their original rules.

          Current ranks by the standing rating; Today, Last 7 days and Last 30 days rank by how far the rating moved inside that window (UTC days, each window including today), and a losing window is listed rather than hidden.

          Only your first answer to each quiz question counts, up to 40 answers a UTC day, and answers on a concept you have recently shown you know count for less: if your best AI check on it in the last 30 days was 3 of 3, a correct basic, standard or challenge answer at 1200 adds only about 1, 2 or 3, and 2 of 3 counts three-quarters as much;

          a session that recorded only a score counts each of its answers once at the standard tier; the same two players are rated at most three times a week; unfinished duels with no result change nothing.

          One rated result is enough to be listed, and a rating under ten results is marked provisional because an Elo number means little that early. Quiz answers are checked in your browser, so treat the rating as a friendly learning signal, not an exam grade. Public rankings update after cloud sync.

          UTC monthly champions. Every tie shares the honour.

          #LearnerEOR Rating

            Collection value

            Collection value estimates permanently owned items at current, undiscounted market prices.

            Current market value of permanently owned items, including gifts, at undiscounted prices. Daily discounts, temporary trials and already-activated consumables do not count.

            Today, Last 7 days and Last 30 days rank the net change in total value, including market-price rises and falls; today starts at 00:00 UTC and the longer windows include today.

            When a window starts before valuation tracking began, its change is measured from the first recorded valuation and the shorter coverage is labelled; earlier market values cannot be reconstructed.

            Public rankings update after cloud sync.

            UTC monthly champions. Every tie shares the honour.

            #LearnerCollection value
              About Collection Value and learner interactions

              Collection Value replaces Biggest Spenders. It adds up the current market value of permanently owned or unlocked shop items, including gifts and treasure rewards, before any daily discount. Each permanent unlock counts once. Temporary trials and boosts that activate on purchase are excluded. Refunded or revoked items no longer count; no EORbits balance or past purchase price is added.

              The three learner boards open on their overall standing: All time for Most active users, and Current for EOR Rating and Collection Value.

              For Collection Value, Current shows the total valuation. Today, Last 7 days and Last 30 days show its net change, including market-price increases and decreases even when the collection stays the same. Windows use UTC, with the opening valuation taken immediately before the first day begins. Negative changes remain visible. Historical market valuations were not previously recorded. If a window starts before tracking began, it shows the actual change since the first recorded valuation, with that starting date clearly labelled. It automatically becomes a full-window comparison once enough history exists; missing values are never treated as zero. Existing spending honours retain their original historical meaning.

              For an existing study connection, the ranking row offers Applaud instead of another connection request. Choose a milestone to send applause; repeated applause for the same milestone sends only one notification. Incoming and outgoing connection requests are labelled rather than sent again.
